During this early postnatal phase, the neonate is entirely dependent on its mother for warmth, nutrition, and protection, lacking the physiological capacity for independent thermoregulation. This altricial strategy allows the mother to reduce the energetic burden of a long pregnancy, instead shifting the costs of offspring development to the more flexible lactation phase. The extraordinarily low birth mass, less than one gram, stands in stark contrast to the substantial body size the animal will eventually achieve as a breeding adult, highlighting the dramatic ontogenetic transformation that characterizes the life history of this arboreal folivore. Such a strategy is typical of arboreal folivores that inhabit relatively stable but resource-predictable environments, where adult survival is high and competition for territories is intense.
